newsitem.title: UK: Minorco confirms may bid for Brazil's CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Minorco confirms may bid for Brazil's CVRD.

text.p: Minorco SA, the conglomerate controlled by Anglo American and De Beers, confirmed it might make a bid for Brazil's Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) when it is partially privatised on April 29.
"We are having a look at CVRD in Brazil...and there is a chance that we might be bidding," Minorco chief executive Hank Slack told Reuters Financial Television.
In a programme to be broadcast later today, Slack said Minorco had several other potential acquisitions in mind, but he declined to elaborate.
"There are some in the pipeline," he said.

There has already been talk in Brazil that Anglo American, directly or through Minorco, might team up with Brazil's Votorantim to bid for CVRD. A block of 45 percent of voting shares in the state-owned mining group is being sold off at a base price of 3.0 billion reais.
Minorco earlier reported a nine percent increase in 1996 net earnings to $396.4 million despite weak commodity prices.
Slack said the outlook for paper prices remained poor this year, but he added the market weakness provided Minorco with opportunities to grow at the same time.
As an example he cited last year's purchase by Minorco and Anglo American of a 28 percent stake in Aracruz Celloluse SA. "That is just the sort of thing we'll seek to do," said Slack.
Finance director David Fisher said Minorco was pleasantly surprised by the current copper price strength after last year's slump, but he saw prices retreat again by the end of 1997.
"There is this overhang of increased supply, but it is increasingly likely that the impact of that will be towards the end of this year and the beginning of next," he said.
Fisher added he did not expect any significant rise in gold prices. "We are certainly not building into our plans any strong increase in the gold price this year," he said.
Higher production helped Minorco to post higher 1996 profits in nearly all of its business segments, with the notable execption of its agriculture business.
Here operating profits fell to $311.9 milion from $387.1 million as U.S. fertiliser producer Terra International suffered from an expected fall in methanol prices.
But Slack emphasized that Terra had still posted its second best result ever, adding that Minorco remained fully committed to the business.
"It is a growing business...and I would envisage that in the years ahead it will expand outside the United States," he said.
